lifecycle.proposed: status PROPOSED, gateStatus NOT-MET, capacity and every ceiling PROPOSED, no acceptance record. This is the state committed in the R0 pull request and in the merge commit that freezes it.
lifecycle.acceptanceWriteBack: The first commit after the R0 merge is an acceptance write-back PR. It records amendment version 1.0.1 (afterDecisionBearingInspection false, justification 'acceptance write-back') and an acceptance object { mergeCommit: full SHA of the R0 merge on main, mergedAtUtc, pr }; sets contractVersion 1.0.1, status FROZEN, gateStatus MET, and capacity and every ceiling ACCEPTED with the merged values; sets the inventory contractVersion to 1.0.1; updates the document's version, status, and gate line and its amendment log to match; and updates sha256.json. It changes nothing else. The merge commit is the freeze identity; the write-back only records it.
lifecycle.proposedState: status PROPOSED requires gateStatus NOT-MET, capacity and every ceiling PROPOSED, and no acceptance record (validator C008, C012).
lifecycle.frozen: status FROZEN requires gateStatus MET, capacity and every ceiling ACCEPTED, and a complete acceptance record (validator C012). R0 is MET only in this state, and no downstream 0.24 gate starts before the write-back merges.

outcomeVocabulary.source: src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/ProofOutcome.cs (ProofStatus, ProofOutcome.IsVacuous, ToContractStatus, ToObligationStatus, ToImplicationStatus), Verification/Z3/Z3ImplicationProver.cs (ContractVerificationStatus, ImplicationStatus), Verification/Obligations/ObligationTracker.cs (ObligationStatus), CodeGen/CSharpEmitter.cs (guard elision). Verification/Z3/KInduction/KInductionProver.cs (KInductionStatus) is also mapped: when VerificationAnalysisOptions.EnableKInduction is set (off by default; on in VerificationAnalysisOptions.Thorough), Analysis/VerificationAnalysisPass.cs runs LoopAnalysisRunner during compilation and a Proven result becomes a Calor0950 LoopInvariantSynthesized info diagnostic. That path emits diagnostics only; it removes no runtime guard. The legacy enums are lossy (several ProofStatus values map to one legacy value), so every code status is named by at least one token, and consumers read ProofOutcome rather than the legacy enum to tell Assumed from TimeoutOrUnavailable.

conditions: Produced on the frozen #1423 candidate by a registered producer.
The modeled form has no unresolved false unconditional proof under #1413.
An independent behavioral oracle agrees (#1311); the verifier's simplifier or translator is not the sole oracle.
TranslatorSemanticsVersion equals the candidate's ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion; cache entries from another version are not evidence.
Non-vacuous.
Holds only because the precondition set is unsatisfiable. The emitter keeps the guard.
All Proven conditions apply.

The obligation channel carries no vacuity flag: ObligationSolver never assigns ProofEvidence.VacuousProof. A Discharged row establishes only when its #1419 registration records a passing non-vacuity check for that row.
Guard removal additionally requires ElideProvenGuards and an ObligationPolicy action that does not require a guard.
Conditional on named assumptions. Never aggregates into Proven (guarantees plan D-G2.2).
A refusal. It validates a registered refusal/demotion row only; it is never a proof.
Inconclusive or no solver. ObligationStatus.Timeout is a legacy bucket that also receives Assumed and Unavailable; consumers must read ProofOutcome to distinguish them.
Establishes no positive property. A refutation of a property the independent oracle shows true is a completeness defect and still needs a #1413 disposition.
Never solver-checked. Listed so that no status the code can emit is unclassified.

outcomeVocabulary.rowStatusRule: Every non-outcome row status is not established. An unknown token fails validation; it is never mapped to a known status.
outcomeVocabulary.falseUnconditionalProof: A row whose outcome is Proven or Discharged (non-vacuous) while an independent oracle exhibits a concrete modeled input that violates the claimed property. It is release-blocking for the affected modeled form until fixed or visibly demoted. Retaining a runtime guard does not make it acceptable.

establishedRowFields.rule: A row counted established must carry every field below; an absent field is a violation, never a default (validator E013/E014).
fields: registrationId: the #1419 (or owning gate) registration entry that names the row's producer and case.
producer: the registered producer that emitted the outcome.
oracle: { id, agrees: true } — the independent behavioral oracle and its verdict.
translatorSemanticsVersion: equal to the frozen candidate's ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion.
unresolvedFalseProof: false — no unresolved #1413 false unconditional proof for the row's modeled form.
nonVacuityCheck: { id, result: 'passed' } — required for Discharged.
openDefectsResolvedBy: one merged PR number per open defect the inventory records for the cited artifact.

classifications.authoritative: The single canonical record a gate or public surface reads. It has a recorded regeneration command and a durable provenance identity. It may carry open defects; open defects block establishment until closed.
classifications.derived: Computed or rendered from inventoried artifacts listed in derivedFrom. It has a regeneration command. It inherits staleness: a derived artifact with a stale input is itself stale.
classifications.historical-only: A retained record of a past measurement or publication. It is never regenerated in place and never establishes a 0.24 claim.
classifications.stale: Known not to match its producer at the cutoff, or known not to establish what its name or description claims. It may not be consumed as evidence until repaired and regenerated.

reclassificationRule: The inventory is frozen at the cutoff. A repaired stale artifact becomes authoritative or derived only through a versioned amendment that names the repairing PR; the validator reads the amended inventory. A classification never changes silently.

benchmarkEquivalence.registrationRule: Before #1276 repairs any pair, executes any differential check, or recomputes any metric, it merges a versioned benchmark registration that pins: the complete initial pair denominator (every pair at the cutoff, by path and SHA-256), each pair's task statement, input set, expected outputs, and failure behavior, the differential oracle and its command, the metric set and metric implementation version, the aggregation and interval method, and every pre-registered exclusion with its reason. Dispositions are assigned only after that merge, by executing the registered oracle. Any later change to a pinned field is a #1407 amendment; a pair dropped or re-dispositioned after registration stays reported with its previous disposition.
benchmarkEquivalence.pairRowTypeRule: Fields in pairRowStringFields are non-empty JSON strings; *Sha256 fields are 64 lowercase hex digits; the remaining required fields are non-empty strings, objects, or arrays; included is a JSON boolean. The comparability key's samplingUnit equals samplingUnit.
benchmarkEquivalence.equivalenceDefinition: Both sides implement the same task statement, accept the same inputs, produce the same outputs, and fail on the same inputs in the same observable way. Evidence is an executed differential check, not inspection of names.

taskStatementRule.rule: 'Implement the same task statement' means both sides of a pair share one registered task statement (one taskStatementSha256) and exhibit the same observable behavior under the registered differential oracle: the same accepted inputs, the same outputs, and the same failures on the same inputs. Equivalence does not assert that either side is correct with respect to the statement. Correctness with respect to the statement is outside #1276's scope, and no published benchmark text, headline, table, or release note may state or imply it.
taskStatementRule.expectedOutputsConsequence: Under this reading the registered expectedOutputs of a pair may be the cross-arm agreement rule of the registered oracle (each side's observed output is the expected output of the other side) with no golden values. Every other pinned field in registrationRule is unchanged and still pinned before the oracle runs.
taskStatementRule.declinedReading: The stricter reading, per-pair expected-behavior assertions that check each side against its statement, was considered and declined. A fair size and token comparison needs behavioral identity between the two sides, which the differential oracle establishes; it does not need conformance to the statement. Conformance would be a separate correctness claim, and 0.24 makes no such claim. Adopting the stricter reading later is a #1407 amendment made before the registered oracle runs.

benchmarkEquivalence.inclusionRule: Only EQUIVALENT pairs enter comparative metrics. An included UNCLASSIFIED pair blocks headline generation. NOT-EQUIVALENT and EXCLUDED-PRE-REGISTERED pairs are counted and published in the denominator, never silently dropped. A pair whose either side fails to parse or compile is NOT-EQUIVALENT unless its registered failure behavior says otherwise.
benchmarkEquivalence.comparabilityRule: Two results are comparable only when every comparabilityKey field is equal. Otherwise no delta, ratio change, or advantage movement is printed; the result is labeled incomparable, and a method change needs a previously merged #1407 amendment.
benchmarkEquivalence.intervalRule: Uncertainty is computed only by resampling over independent program pairs. Repeated runs of a deterministic calculator are a determinism check (all runs must agree), not samples. A category with fewer than 2 included pairs reports no interval. Because the corpus is a fixed, non-random set, any interval describes corpus-resampling sensitivity of this corpus only and must be labeled so.
benchmarkEquivalence.claimRule: Static feature scores are not coding-agent outcomes. Neither is presented as a measured language, productivity, correctness, or safety advantage. An EQUIVALENT disposition is never presented as evidence that either side is correct with respect to its task statement (taskStatementRule, amendment 1.1.0).

provenanceIdentity.commitRule: A full 40-hex commit that is an ancestor of explicitly fetched refs/remotes/origin/main, or the target of an immutable release tag.
provenanceIdentity.treeRule: Claimed source, corpus, configuration, and generated-input identities are verified by tree or content hash (git rev-parse <commit>:<path>, SHA-256 of manifests). Reachability alone is insufficient.
provenanceIdentity.squashRule: When the final squash commit cannot exist before merge, either (a) merge with a merge commit that keeps the measured commit as an ancestor of main, or (b) record a pending phase-1 identity (PR head commit plus tree hashes) and complete it with a post-merge write-back that records the main commit and re-verifies tree equality. A phase-1 identity is not authoritative.
provenanceIdentity.shallowCloneRule: Authoritative validation fails, not skips, in a shallow or unfetched clone. Producers fetch the bounded history and tags they need.
provenanceIdentity.historicalRule: Existing measuredCommit stamps stay unchanged. A durable identity is recorded beside them, never written over them.

releasePath.publicationSeparation: Regeneration never publishes. #1424 regenerates publication surfaces only as unpublished candidates with content hashes: candidate-packages (packed, not pushed), release metadata generated from them, the website built but not deployed, and release notes rendered but not posted. Registry push, GitHub release creation, release-asset upload, and Pages deployment are publication; they happen only after #1408 records MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED, through the #1410 gate, and consume the exact adjudicated hashes. nuget-packages is therefore never regenerated by #1424. Pinned inputs (z3-release-binaries, z3-upstream-pins, toolchain-pins, corpus-submodules) are re-materialized and checksum-verified, never rebuilt or republished; no regeneration command may run a workflow that pushes packages, creates or edits a release, uploads release assets, opens a publication PR, commits to main, or deploys. Uploading Actions artifacts to retain evidence is not publication. The only exception is the documentation-only website deploy defined in documentationOnlyDeploy (amendment 1.1.0); it is not regeneration, is not adjudicated, and publishes nothing else.

documentationOnlyDeploy.rule: Before #1408 records MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED, .github/workflows/nextjs-gh-pages.yml may deploy the website without an adjudication identity only for a documentation-only change, and only when the #1410 verifier proves every condition below. Every other website deployment stays blocked until #1408 records MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED and then consumes one matching adjudication identity through the #1410 gate. The classifier fails closed: a path it cannot classify, a base it cannot establish, a check it cannot complete, or any API or git failure refuses the deploy.
documentationOnlyDeploy.window: Open while no #1408 terminal record with outcome MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED exists on protected main. A documentation-only deploy is never evidence and never an adjudication. It does not repair or reclassify the website-deployment or website-benchmark-pages artifacts, which stay stale, and it does not count as a release surface consuming an adjudication identity for terminal condition 7.
documentationOnlyDeploy.noOtherPublication: The deploying run creates no package, GitHub release, tag, or release asset; changes no benchmark data and no release notes; and changes no claim or number about 0.24 evidence, verification results, or a Calor advantage.
documentationOnlyDeploy.wordingRule: No changed path may contain, anywhere in the file (prose, code, or markup, after the #1410 normalization), the word 'independent' or 'independently' followed by any form of 'adjudicat' or 'verif' within the next two words, whether negated or not. The built site as a whole must also pass the #1410 wording scan. The negation allowance of the #1410 scan does not apply to changed paths.
documentationOnlyDeploy.buildInputsRule: The documentation diff is taken over every content build input. At the cutoff the website build (npm ci, npm run build in website/) reads only files under website/, including website/public/data/** through src/components imports. If the build reads any path outside buildInputs and machinery, the classifier refuses until an amendment adds that path.

paths: every script, composite action, and configuration file that workflow invokes, enumerated by #1410's verifier
machinery.rule: Machinery is never documentation. A machinery change since the base is allowed only when it reached protected main through a merged pull request reviewed by the maintainer; the audit record lists each changed machinery path with that PR (machineryChanges), and the verifier refuses an unlisted change, a listed PR that is not merged into main, and any path the build reads that is neither under buildInputs nor enumerated machinery. The machinery's integrity therefore rests on reviewed merges to protected main, as for every other #1410 gate; no website/ path (including package files, components, and data) is machinery.

documentationOnlyDeploy.pathRule: A changed path (added, modified, deleted, or either side of a rename, from git diff --no-renames --name-only <base> <deployed> -- <buildInputs>) is documentation-only when it matches an allowedPaths pattern, matches no deniedPaths pattern, is not a path of any inventory artifact, and contains no '..' segment. Patterns are case-sensitive globs: '**/' matches zero or more directories and '*' matches within one path segment. Everything else under buildInputs (website/src/**, website/public/**, package files, configuration, tests) is not documentation-only.
documentationOnlyDeploy.fileRule: Every added or modified changed path is a regular, non-executable file at the deployed commit (git mode 100644); a symlink, submodule, or executable file refuses.
documentationOnlyDeploy.mdxRule: MDX is compiled, so a changed page may only carry documentation. In its added or modified lines, outside fenced code blocks and inline code spans, a changed .mdx file contains no import or export statement, no JavaScript expression in braces, and no JSX element other than the components registered in website/src/components/mdx at the base commit and plain HTML elements other than script, iframe, object, embed, style, and link.

base.rule: The diff base is the source commit of the most recent website deployment, which must be one of: the last deployment before this contract (preContractDeploy), a documentation-only deployment whose audit record is committed on protected main with status deployed, or a deployment that consumed an adjudication identity through the #1410 gate (none can precede a documentation-only deploy inside the window under this amendment; the kind is listed so the base rule is total). If GitHub reports a successful github-pages deployment newer than the base that has neither a committed deployed audit record nor an adjudication identity, the classifier refuses.

auditRecord.location: docs/plans/evidence/r2-1410/docs-deploys/<deployedCommit>.json on protected main, in two reviewed phases. Authorization: before dispatch, a reviewed PR commits the record with status 'authorized' and every field except runId; the deploying run refuses unless that record is on protected main and its deployedCommit, base, changedPaths, and machineryChanges equal the run's own recomputation. Completion: after the run, a reviewed PR sets status 'deployed' and runId and changes nothing else. An authorized record without completion cannot serve as a base, so the next documentation-only deploy refuses until the completion merges. The run's Actions-artifact copy is not durable and is not the record.

status: authorized | deployed
contractVersion: a contractVersion recorded in the amendment log, 1.1.0 or later, in force at the deploy
workflow: .github/workflows/nextjs-gh-pages.yml

auditRecord.attestationStatement: This deploy changes no claim or number about 0.24 evidence, verification results, or a Calor advantage.
auditRecord.enforcedBy: EvidenceContractValidator.ValidateDocsDeployAudit (D001-D006) checks the record's shape and re-classifies every changedPaths entry against this contract and the inventory; it does not re-run git. The #1410 verifier recomputes the diff and every check from git and the GitHub API.

verifierChecks: The run is a workflow_dispatch from refs/heads/main; the deployed commit is a full SHA that is an ancestor of fetched refs/remotes/origin/main (provenanceIdentity commitRule), and the clone is not shallow.
No #1408 terminal record with outcome MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED exists on protected main.
An authorized audit record for the deployed commit is on protected main and matches the run's recomputation.
The base satisfies base.rule; a successful github-pages deployment newer than the base without a committed deployed audit record or adjudication identity refuses.
Every path in git diff --no-renames --name-only <base> <deployed> -- website/ satisfies pathRule, fileRule, and mdxRule; any other path refuses.
Every machinery path changed since the base is listed in machineryChanges with a merged, maintainer-reviewed PR; the build reads nothing outside buildInputs and the enumerated machinery.
Every changed path passes wordingRule, and the built site passes the #1410 wording scan.
The run has no step that pushes a package, creates or edits a release or tag, uploads a release asset, opens a publication PR, or commits to main.
The deployed Pages artifact is the one built from deployedCommit, and the completion record passes ValidateDocsDeployAudit.
Negative tests for each check above are part of #1410's closure evidence.

statusChecks.note: tests (verification) carries the #1135 oracle and is release-critical in eng/test-manifest.json, but it is not a required check. Admins can bypass required checks.

retention.actionsArtifacts: Per upload step: 14, 30, or 90 days. Never authoritative.
retention.releaseAssets: Durable until deleted; release notes and assets are mutable (gh release upload --clobber).

rules.falseProof: A concrete false unconditional proof is release-blocking for the affected modeled form until fixed or visibly demoted. A retained runtime guard does not cure it.
rules.missingness: Unknown, unsupported, unavailable, skipped, timed-out, flaky, stale, invalid, historical, incomparable, and uninvestigated rows are not established.
rules.historical: Corrected published artifacts are retained as historical records. They are not rewritten to look as if the repaired method produced them.
rules.amendment: Any scope or rule change after decision-bearing inspection is a versioned amendment with a justification and a reviewed PR. It cannot remove a failing row; removed rows stay reported with their last status.
rules.discovery: Discovery may create bounded repair issues within the accepted capacity. Every finding is fixed, visibly demoted, excluded by this pre-registered scope, or makes the milestone fail. It cannot become ordinary follow-up while 0.24 is reported as successful.
rules.retrospective: Evidence recorded at or before the cutoff is retrospective. It is a control, never confirmatory 0.24 evidence by itself.
rules.platformDeterminism: Platform (operating system and runtime identifier) is a determinism dimension (amendment 1.1.0). A verifier verdict, translator output, or committed oracle report that differs by platform on the same tree is verdict instability. It is release-blocking for the affected modeled form until resolved under these rules (fixed, or visibly demoted under #1413), exactly like any other verdict instability. Deselecting a case on a platform, as G1's z3-consumer-matrix does, is never a resolution and never makes the case established on that platform. The registered rows are in determinismRows.
stopping: A ceiling in capacity is reached: stop the gate, record the overrun, and either merge a reviewed amendment raising the ceiling before more work or record the gate BLOCKED.
#1311 reaches its timebox: stop, publish the report; unreached rows are not-investigated; an unreached row registered as release-critical is BLOCKED.
A false unconditional proof cannot be fixed or demoted within capacity: MILESTONE-FAILED.
The frozen candidate changes after #1423: all downstream evidence is invalid; return to #1423.
Adjudication as defined in authorityCapacity (the named adjudicator under the recorded independence deviation) is unavailable: MILESTONE-FAILED or a self-adjudicated non-release record.

terminalSuccess.rule: #1408 records MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED only when every condition below holds; otherwise it records MILESTONE-FAILED. #1408 does not add, drop, or weaken a condition; a change is a #1407 amendment made before the #1424 raw-artifact freeze.
conditions: Every child in children other than #1408 itself is closed with its closureEvidence.
Every #1419-registered release-critical row, for B1 and for N1, has an outcome or row status; none is BLOCKED, not-investigated, or unclassified.

No #1408 adjudication row for any release-critical artifact, gate, or claim is BLOCKED. Required evidence that is missing, inconclusive, stale, or incomparable makes its row BLOCKED, never HISTORICAL-ONLY or BOUNDED (validator T001).
Zero unresolved false unconditional proofs: every one is fixed or visibly demoted under #1413.
Every #1413 finding has a findingDisposition other than NOT-INVESTIGATED or MILESTONE-FAILED.
Every authoritative and derived inventory artifact was regenerated by #1424 on the frozen #1423 candidate, with no stale input.

Every release surface in releasePath consumes one matching adjudication identity (#1410 negative tests pass). The only path that publishes without one is releasePath.documentationOnlyDeploy, inside its window, and its negative tests are part of #1410's.
Every adjudication row records independence = reduced-maintainer-adjudicated and no row is SUPPORTED while the deviation stands (validator T002).
No capacity ceiling was exceeded without a merged amendment raising it.
terminalSuccess.requiredSubjects: The terminal record adjudicates every subject exactly once: every artifact id in the (amended) inventory, one 'gate:#<issue>' row per child other than #1408, and one 'claim:<id>' row per registered claim. Every subject is release-critical; criticality is fixed by the contract, not by the record. HISTORICAL-ONLY is valid only for an artifact classified historical-only in the inventory, and an artifact still classified stale can only be BLOCKED. A missing, duplicate, unknown, or unregistered subject, or an improper HISTORICAL-ONLY or non-BLOCKED stale adjudication, fails (validator T001, T003).
terminalSuccess.claimRegistry: At the #1424 raw-artifact freeze, #1424 commits the list of claim ids that #1408 will adjudicate (every public or release claim the milestone intends to make). #1408 adjudicates exactly that list; it cannot add, drop, or rename a claim. The registry is passed to ValidateTerminalRecord.
terminalSuccess.underDeviation: Under the recorded independence deviation a MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED record carries adjudicationIndependence = reduced, limitation equal to authorityCapacity.independence.publishedLimitation, and epicIndependentAdjudicationMet = false (validator T002), and states that the epic's 'independently adjudicated' outcome is not met. It authorizes no claim of independent adjudication or verification.

authorityCapacity.implementationOwners: Claude Code agents. One branch and one PR per issue. Agents never merge.

independence.rule: Epic rule 10 and #1408: the adjudicator cannot have implemented the producer or repair, cannot change #1407 rules, and needs an independent approving review.
independence.deviationStatement: @juanmicrosoft is the #1408 adjudicator and approving reviewer. The maintainer did not write the repairs (agents did), but directs, reviews, and merges them and also holds decision and amendment authority. Independence is reduced.
consequences: Every adjudication row records independence = reduced-maintainer-adjudicated.

No row may be SUPPORTED; the maximum is BOUNDED with the published limitation 'adjudicated by the maintainer who directed and merged the repairs; not independently adjudicated'. This follows #1408's own rule for unavailable independent review.
A MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED record must carry adjudicationIndependence = reduced. No public surface may call 0.24 evidence independently adjudicated or independently verified.
From the #1424 raw-artifact freeze until #1408 closes, amendment authority is not exercised; an amendment in that window invalidates affected evidence and returns to #1423.
independence.publishedLimitation: adjudicated by the maintainer who directed and merged the repairs; not independently adjudicated
independence.amendable: A versioned amendment may name an independent reviewer who neither implemented, directed, nor merged the producer or repair. It lifts the cap only for rows that reviewer adjudicates after the amendment; earlier rows are re-adjudicated, not relabeled.

capacity.acceptance: PROPOSED — pending maintainer acceptance in PR review. Accepted only when the maintainer merges this contract. No downstream gate starts before acceptance.

exceptions.justification: B1 registration PR #1473 overran the pr-size ceiling by 20 lines (1,520 changed lines excluding docs/plans/evidence/) when it fixed a BLOCKING defect found by a verification-only review after review round 3: round 3 made --output required on pair-oracle, but the per-pair child invocation omits it, so every child run would fail argument parsing and every pair would become ORACLE_CRASH, including the known witness DomainProblems/CsvParser. The fix makes --output required only for the parent run (enforced in the handler), extracts the child command line into PairOracleCommand.ChildArguments, adds one mutation-checked regression test (ChildCommandLineParsesWithoutParentOnlyOptions), and re-pins the oracle hash in the unmerged registration packet. No pair was run. Recorded under stopping rule 1; the ceiling is raised for PR #1473 only, and no other ceiling or PR changes.

capacity.evidenceDataRule: For the pr-size ceiling, committed evidence data includes a gate's machine-readable closure inventory when the gate's closureEvidence in children names that inventory (for G1 #1420, the consumer and RID inventory eng/z3-consumers.json). The exclusion covers data files only: scripts, tests, workflows, and code that read the inventory still count (amendment 1.1.0).
capacity.estimateNote: The ordinary-ci ceiling assumes roughly 250 runner-minutes per full test.yml push. That figure is an unmeasured estimate.

children.closureEvidence: Merged versioned registration and a complete initial row manifest for each investigated baseline, B1 and N1 as separate rows that are never pooled (entry points, case IDs, source hashes, oracle, controls, row classes, release-critical marks, timebox and compute within s1 ceilings) committed before any decision-bearing sweep result.

Every registered row for both B1 and N1 executed or recorded not-investigated within the s1 ceilings, which cover the combined B1 and N1 work; archived probes, independent-oracle results, controls, and a reproducible report, including zero-finding and timebox-stopped outcomes.

One reviewed disposition per row and witness from findingDispositions; accepted repairs within s2 ceilings attached to #1409 and blocking #1423; no unresolved false unconditional proof keeps guard-removal or claim eligibility.
Consumer and RID inventory; no unowned Z3 seeding workaround; no implicit network download; discriminating fresh-checkout tests for absent, wrong, and propagated assets.

Merged machine-readable determinism protocol (case IDs, environment pins, run count, timeouts, retry and failure rules) within the determinism-compute ceiling, before decision-bearing runs. The protocol treats platform as a determinism dimension and registers every determinismRows entry (amendment 1.1.0).

Repaired oracle executed under the #1421 protocol with every attempt retained and agreement under the frozen failure rule, on every platform the protocol registers; every determinismRows entry is resolved under rules.platformDeterminism (amendment 1.1.0).

Checkout-pinned Tier 2 run with explicit positive/negative/multifile expectations, no build-output duplicates, no empty advertised selections, AST-roundtrip claims matching the work performed, and negative self-tests.

Fresh-clone resolution of every authoritative identity after squash merge; failing tests for branch-only replacement, false identical-tree claims, and shallow-clone skips; historical stamps unchanged.

A benchmark registration per benchmarkEquivalence.registrationRule merged before any repair, differential check, or recomputation; then a content-addressed pair manifest with every benchmarkEquivalence pair field and a disposition produced by the registered oracle for every registered pair, the declared sampling unit and population, and historical artifacts left historical.
End-to-end tests: refusal fails the workflow and leaves no publication PR; unclassified or changed pairs block headlines; methodology change needs a prior amendment, not a workflow input.

Negative tests proving release, package, website, notes, and benchmark publication cannot proceed without one matching successful adjudication identity; GitHub release created only after adjudication. For the documentation-only website deploy (releasePath.documentationOnlyDeploy, amendment 1.1.0): an implementation of every verifierChecks entry with a negative test for each, and an audit record per deploy.
Committed immutable candidate manifest including the SHA-256 of this contract packet (sha256.json) and its amendment log; tested invalidation classifier.

Every authoritative and derived inventory artifact regenerated on the candidate (publication surfaces only as unpublished candidates per releasePath.publicationSeparation; #1424 publishes nothing) within the regeneration ceilings, all attempts retained in durable storage, fresh-clone reproduction of the deterministic subset.
One adjudication outcome per registered artifact and claim, capped at BOUNDED under the recorded independence deviation, and a machine-readable terminal record.

determinismRows.rule: rules.platformDeterminism. Each row is release-blocking for the affected modeled form or artifact until resolved under the section 8 rules. #1421 registers each row in its protocol before decision-bearing runs; #1135 resolves each row and retains every attempt. A row caused only by a line-ending or fixture-encoding difference is resolved by a repair that makes the bytes platform-independent, never by a per-platform baseline.

retrospective.repaired: ContractTranslator translates unsigned literals through UnsignedValue into unsigned bit-vectors and applies C# numeric promotions; NumericExecutableSemanticsTests adds a runtime differential promotion matrix including u64 0, 1, ulong.MaxValue.
retrospective.residual: #845 is still open and its named regression (a ULONG: contract bound near ulong.MaxValue that proves when satisfiable and refutes when violated) is not identified as a closing test. ExpressionSimplifier folds unary Negate and BitwiseNot over IntLiteralNode without checking IsUnsigned or IsLong; whether that reaches an established proof was NOT executed here, to keep R1 preregistered.

amendmentLog.justification: Maintainer decisions approved 2026-10-02 by @juanmicrosoft on findings from open gate PRs R2 #1474/#1475, G1 #1471, P1 #1472, and B1 #1473: (1) a documentation-only website deploy path before #1408 succeeds (releasePath.documentationOnlyDeploy); (2) the B1 task-statement reading (benchmarkEquivalence.taskStatementRule), resolving B1 review round 2 BLOCKING #1; (3) pending inventory updates from G1 #1471 and P1 #1472, applied by a write-back after each PR merges (inventory pendingUpdates); (4) a gate's machine-readable closure inventory counts as evidence data for the pr-size ceiling (capacity.evidenceDataRule); (5) G1's Windows-only verifier divergences routed to #1421/#1135 as release-blocking determinism rows (rules.platformDeterminism, determinismRows); (6) the pr-size ceiling raised to 1,520 changed lines for B1 PR #1473 only, recording its 20-line overrun under stopping rule 1 (capacity.exceptions).
amendmentLog.inspectionStatement: No decision follows decision-bearing inspection. At this amendment no #1419 registration or #1311 sweep result exists, the #1276 registration is unmerged and its oracle has not run (every registered pair is UNCLASSIFIED, pending-oracle), and no #1421 or #1135 protocol run exists. The three Windows observations in decision 5 come from G1's consumer-matrix CI run 37020428891, not from a determinism protocol; decision 5 only adds release-blocking rows and removes no requirement. Decision 6 follows a code review of B1's oracle command line, not an oracle run: no pair has been run.
weakens: Decision 1 narrows releasePath.publicationSeparation: before this amendment no Pages deployment could happen before #1408 records MILESTONE-SUCCEEDED; after it, a documentation-only deploy that meets documentationOnlyDeploy can.
Decision 4 widens the pr-size exclusion to a gate's machine-readable closure inventory named in its closureEvidence.
Decision 6 raises the pr-size ceiling from 1,500 to 1,520 changed lines for PR #1473 only.

Decision 2 fixes the reading of 'implement the same task statement': EQUIVALENT does not mean correct with respect to the statement, and registered expected outputs may be the oracle's cross-arm agreement rule. The definition text is unchanged.
